styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single-tile grey mailbox panel with a bluish-grey outline and a grid of slots. The measured outline is tinted (0% near-neutral dark edge pixels), so it is not a black sticker line. It shows 8 visible tones per tile against 9 for prop-hedge, which is the closest reference in size, and 0% near-flat coverage. The slots, header strip and frame show about 5 lightness steps, with highlight edges and per-slot shading. It is plainly less rich than the large stall and well references (17-20 tones), but it is a small, simple object, and it matches the hedge on the primary facts. By eye the grid and trim read as deliberate detail, not flat fills. The main weakness is the fairly uniform grey body, which keeps it slightly below the references.
